sources.title: Stardew Valley creator's new game, Haunted Chocolatier, is "more of an action RPG" than farming sim
sources.text: "It's for the people that go into the mines." Stardew Valley creator Eric Barone, has given a new interview - and finally revealed a little more information about his upcoming title, Haunted Chocolatier. In a wide-ranging interview with GQ , which tackles topics ranging from creative burnout to the importance of 'cosy gaming', Barone also slips in some new information about what we can expect from his highly-anticipated Stardew Valley follow-up. And it's all rather surprising. Per the interview, this game is a much more action-oriented affair than the cosy homesteading of Stardew Valley: "It is still what I call a town game," he told GQ, "but it's more of an action RPG - the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights." For anyone that's played Stardew Valley, this won't be a massive shock; there is a combat element to the game, though mostly it's sequestered to one portion of the map - the mines that hold some of the game's rarest materials. If you had fun venturing in there at night to fight slimes and horde minerals, you're going to like Haunted Chocolatier, it seems. "[The new game] is for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly," said Barone. Elsewhere, Barone noted that Haunted Chocolatier is a more "metaphysical" experience than Stardew Valley - which makes sense, I suppose, given its connection to the world of ghosts and spirits - and that "no one's playing the game until I'm ready to show it". Hence, there's still no word on a solid release date. The last update we had on the game was all the way back in January, where Barone noted "I'm alive, the game is still in development" , following up previous statements he made alluding to the fact that the world of Haunted Chocolatier is bigger than Stardew Valley. As for when it's coming out? "The bottom line is, I don’t want to give a release date," Barone said at the start of the year. "The game will come out when it's done." If you want to learn more about the man behind one of video gaming's biggest phenomena of the past few generations, I'd urge you to read the full GQ piece: it's a sensitive, comprehensive look at a man that boasts many talents, yet is also humble and grounded. If you're interested in the musical side of his development process, I profiled Barone once in my column at The Guardian.

sources.title: ConcernedApe Teases More Action-RPG Gameplay In Haunted Chocolatier: ‘It’s For The People In Stardew Valley That Go Into The Mines’
sources.text: Action-RPG Haunted Chocolatier Stardew Valley Stardew Valleyâs mines have always been pretty polarizing. Some players love to grind them for endless challenge runs and min-maxing, while die-hard cozy gamers have sworn off them entirely, pledging to stick to farming and fishing and avoiding combat as much as possible. Thanks to a new interview, it now sounds like that former camp will be in luck whenever Haunted Chocolatier , the upcoming game from Stardew developer Eric âConcernedApeâ Barone, launches. In an interview with British GQ , Barone revealed that Haunted Chocolatier âis more of an action RPGâthe main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights. It’s for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines.â Barone clarified that itâll still be what he refers to as a âtown game,â though, likely meaning itâll still revolve around the experience of settling into a new town and getting to know your neighbors as you build up your business. We already knew that Haunted Chocolatier was bound to have in-depth combatâearlier peeks at the game have shown off bosses, enemy-stunning shields, and other off-hand weapons. The game is also slated to have slightly darker themes, and now that Barone has cited David Lynch as an inspiration as well, Iâd count on things being a bit surreal. While speaking to GQ , Barone also briefly touched on the pressure heâs been facing to develop Haunted Chocolatier , which has been in the works for over four years now (that’s almost the same amount of time that Stardew was in development before its release). Barone has yet to announce a release window, likely because the game is set to be âway biggerâ than its predecessorâ¦somehow. âEveryone’s watching me, and if I don’t do things a certain way, it might disappoint millions of people,â he said. Iâm certainly willing to wait as long as Haunted Chocolatier might take to wrap, especially now that I know Iâll have plenty of combat to sink my sweet tooth into. The mines are probably my favorite part of Stardew (although they were definitely an acquired taste). They get pretty repetitive after a while, though, so Iâm excited to see what else Barone does to keep the action fresh in Haunted Chocolatier . Let’s just hope that those terrible spiral-shaped floors don’t make a return. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. stories.title: Sifu será lançado para Android e iOS em outubro; veja trailer do port

sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Sifu será lançado para Android e iOS em outubro; veja trailer do port
sources.text: Sifu , jogo de artes marciais da Sloclap, será lançado para Android e iOS. A desenvolvedora anunciou a versão mobile do game, com estreia prevista para 12 de outubro deste ano. “A mesma ação, a mesma aura, a mesma atmosfera. Agora, na palma da sua mão”, anunciou a Sloclap no X. Na mesma publicação, a empresa anexou um trailer de gameplay da nova versão. A jogatina de Sifu no mobile parece ser idêntica à versão para PC e consoles, com os mesmos cenários, personagens e chefões – portanto, tudo indica que seja um port. No vídeo, são exibidos os botões virtuais adaptados para a tela touchscreen, que permitirão experimentar a porradaria mesmo sem um controle dedicado . Sifu é um jogo de artes marciais com combate rápido, em que o jogador acompanha o protagonista em uma jornada de vingança. O combate é cheio de combos interessantes e marcado pelo forte foco em parries e desvios. Porém, o que deixou Sifu mais relevante é o sistema de vidas. Durante as fases, cada morte do personagem principal não é necessariamente fatal, mas faz com que ele envelheça alguns anos – o que o deixa mais forte com o tempo, mas também mais frágil. O game over acontece quando o protagonista fica velho demais para retornar após uma derrota. Reconhecido jogo de artes marciais da Sloclap, Sifu foi lançado para PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5 e PC em fevereiro de 2022; chegou ao Nintendo Switch meses depois e, em 2023, foi lançado para Xbox One e Xbox Series X | S. O jogo já está listado na App Store e na Play Store. No iOS, vai custar US$ 7,99 (R$ 39,80, em conversão direta) ; no Android, o preço ainda não aparece na loja, mas já é possível fazer o pré-registro, que notifica o usuário quando o jogo estiver pronto para download. O jogo conquistou uma boa nota na análise do Voxl anos atrás . Ao longo do tempo, muito conteúdo foi adicionado ao game, incluindo novas arenas, cosméticos desbloqueáveis e mais desafios que estendem as horas de conteúdo. Quer ficar por dentro das novidades do mundo dos games? Acesse o Voxl e acompanhe as últimas notícias sobre Sifu , jogos mobile e lançamentos. sources.title: REPLACED coming to Android on December 8
sources.text: Publisher Atari and developer Sad Cat Studios will release atmospheric narrative-driven cyberpunk adventure game REPLACED for Android via Google Play on December 8, the companies announced. REPLACED first launched for Xbox Series and PC via Steam , Epic Games Store , Microsoft Store , and GOG on April 14. It is also available via Game Pass. Here is an overview of the game, via Atari: The mobile version is part of the Google Play Games program, offering seamless gaming across mobile, tablets, and PC via a single purchase. The Android version, ported by Poland-based studio The Knights of U, will allow a new audience to experience the same jaw-dropping cinematic visuals and immersive atmosphere that those players loved on its original PC and console release. REPLACED has been played by over 900,000 players across all platforms since its release in Spring 2026. REPLACED is a narrative-driven 2.5D platformer blending cinematic exploration with fluid, free-flow action. Immerse yourself in an alternate 1980s America reshaped by nuclear catastrophe and meet the downtrodden of Phoenix City as you struggle to survive. Soak up the game’s rich atmosphere as you walk the streets of Phoenix-City and become a part of the stories of the citizens you meet in this dark cyberpunk thriller. As you uncover the sinister secrets of Phoenix Corporation, REPLACED explores themes of humanity, identity, and control through morally complex characters and the slow reveal of a world pushed to its limits. Discover a haven for corruption where outlaws thrive and human life is traded like currency as R.E.A.C.H.—an AI trapped in a human body against its will. Expose the Corporation’s hidden agenda, and uncover the purpose behind your creation in a world where every secret—and every life—has a price.

stories.title: ‘I Got That Completely Wrong’ — Dan Houser Considers Rockstar’s Max Payne 3 a Failure
stories.summary: ‘I got that completely wrong’ — Dan Houser explains why he thinks Rockstar’s Max Payne 3 ‘failed’.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: ‘I Got That Completely Wrong’ — Dan Houser Considers Rockstar’s Max Payne 3 a Failure
sources.text: Max Payne and its sequel, Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne, are two of the most genre-defining third-person shooters ever made. They propelled Finnish developer Remedy Entertainment into the spotlight as one of the most exciting studios making games. So, it was also going to be a challenge for another developer to pick up the third part of that trilogy. If you have the likes of Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption under your belt, though, you might just fancy your chances. That’s what former Rockstar VP and writer of Max Payne 3, Dan Houser, thought, and while enjoying the process of making it, he now admits that it didn’t quite hit the mark. Despite being well-received critically, the 2012 game underperformed commercially, and wasn’t a huge hit with players. While Max Payne 3 is a great shooter in its own right, some questioned whether it tonally fit with its heavily noir-influenced predecessors, instead trading in the gloomy, introspective weirdness of Remedy’s New York set games for a more high-octane, colourful, all-action approach. “It was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured,” Houser told IGN as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. “I really enjoyed that as an experience. I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it. “So I got that completely wrong,” Houser admitted. “I know Sam Lake [creator of Max Payne] well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success. The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing.” Max Payne 3 is certainly different in tone to what came before it, but I still hold a lot of love for it. Max Payne 2 remains one of my favourite games to this day due to the storytelling housed in its murky world, but there’s no denying that Rockstar brought something new and flashy to the table almost a decade later when taking the character to Brazil. That bullet time still feels as sweet as ever to trigger, though, and if that level of polish can be brought over to Remedy’s upcoming remakes of the first two in the trilogy, then they can’t come soon enough. We last heard about the project over a year ago, when the studio revealed that it was in “full production” and that the "collaboration with Rockstar Games remains close and productive." Of course, Rockstar currently has its plate very much full with the imminent launch of GTA 6 on November 19. For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson , how the game will tackle the current political climate , and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it . Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Dan Houser Reveals Rockstar’s Struggle to Make Bully
sources.text: Rockstar is gearing up for the launch of GTA 6, but, of course, Grand Theft Auto isn’t the only series the developer is known for. Alongside the likes of the beloved Red Dead Redemption games, there are many fans of another open-world adventure from the studio: Bully. Released in 2006 and originally known in Europe as Canis Canem Edit, Bully tells the story of unruly student Jimmy Hopkins getting in and out of trouble during a year at Bullworth Academy. A smaller-scale, less X-rated version of GTA, it launched to critical acclaim. But the road towards launch was far from easy. “The development was hard,” former Rockstar VP and writer of Bully, Dan Houser, said in a new interview as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. “The game was in trouble all of the time. It was difficult. It was an out-there concept. We were struggling with it. I wasn't sure it was going to be any good. We really wanted it to come together. It was really fun afterwards because it came together really well. The team did a great job. It was a sort of really strong game at the end. It kind of came together very late.” Houser went on to explain why the development of Bully proved such a challenge, coming as it did just over a year after GTA: San Andreas. “New IP is very stressful because you're doing something that no one's ever done before,” he said. “And particularly that game, there was all of this controversy around it to do with the name, or people misunderstood it when they'd never seen it. So I think one of the challenges with that game was it never got the attention it deserved. We were too focused on trying to at least get people to stock it or to not protest it before it even came out.” The mid-2000s was an era when controversy followed Rockstar games whenever one was about to hit store shelves, whether it be the snuff-film-fuelled ultraviolence of Manhunt, or the sex minigame mod, Hot Coffee, uncovered in the code of San Andreas. Bully was no different, with some members of the public worried about how its explicit content would translate into a school setting. “There was huge hysteria around it,” Houser stated. “We had to spend most of 2006 diffusing it, so we couldn't positively promote the game in the way we normally would've done. I think that didn't help it. I mean, that was the same time as Hot Coffee, and it felt like things were imploding. It was very stressful. And just go to work each day, wonder who's protesting you that day, and hope that things can shake out properly. I wasn't directly involved. Luckily, I was just sort of right off to the side, and wasn't directly involved in organizing most of that stuff. But it was really stressful for the people involved.” But it wasn’t just external pressures that made the development of Bully difficult. Rockstar also had to wrestle with how to make its style of open-world action-adventure work from the perspective of a teenager. The school setting meant driving cars and shooting guns had to be parked to one side — two vital gameplay mechanics of any GTA. “Developers were struggling with what the IP was, and we'd made some changes, and some people had moved out there from New York, and it was starting to get a bit better, but it was still really struggling,” revealed Houser. “It was really, well, if you take away the cars and you take away the guns, what is the game? What are you doing? And the lead designer, who was really talented, began to put in the schedule and began to put in the lessons, and it was starting to get there. “Then, one of the designers put this thing where you could stick a Post-it note on the back of a character that said ‘Kick me’ on it. Then an NPC would run up and kick them. And just seeing that work, you're like, that's a great moment. So then you're, okay, we're starting to get somewhere. So I think that moment was probably when I always remember going, this IP that wouldn't work in a GTA, obviously; it's not interesting. But as a kid, and suddenly it was the scale of the school and the scale of a kid's life, it started to feel really fun.” Bully was indeed very fun. So much so that fans have been begging for a sequel ever since. While ideas for a follow-up were once floated around at Rockstar, Houser revealed to IGN in 2025 that it never got off the ground due to “bandwidth issues.” I do miss the days when you’d get a new Rockstar open world to roam around in every year, but I guess at some point I have to give up yearning for the PS2 era. It was 20 years ago, after all. Luckily, Grand Theft Auto 6 is only weeks away from release. For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson , how the game will tackle the current political climate , and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it . sources.title: Max Payne 3 Wasn’t A Big Hit, And Former Rockstar VP And Writer Dan Houser Blames Himself: ‘I Failed’
sources.text: Max Payne 3 launched in 2012 to positive reviews from most critics. But the game didn’t sell nearly as well as other Rockstar titles, and for some fans it wasn’t the sequel they wanted. According to former Rockstar Games vice president and lead writer Dan Houser, the game’s failure is mostly his fault. In a new wide-ranging interview with IGN, Houser talked about his time working on franchises like Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption while at Rockstar Games. He also discussed the less successful third-person shooter, Max Payne 3 . Unlike the previous two entries, which had been developed by Remedy and written by Sam Lake, Max Payne 3 was developed entirely by Rockstar and primarily written by Houser. It also moved the series to the sun-soaked favelas of Brazil and went with a more neo-noir style. âIt was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured,â said Houser. âI really enjoyed that as an experience. I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn’t have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it. So I got that completely wrong,” admitted Houser. While I know some fans of Max Payne weren’t pleased with the tonal shift in Max Payne 3, I think it’s a fantastic game with incredibly snappy and satisfying gunplay and some of the best-looking third-person animations I’ve seen in a shooter. But Max Payne 3 ‘s story and its overall presentation were its weakest elements. And Houser seemingly agrees with me and others who felt let down by the story, writing, and overall vibes of Max Payne 3. âI know Sam Lake [creator of Max Payne ] well, and he’s a very good guy and really talented,” said Houser. “I thought we’d done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn’t. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success. The game is beautifully made, and it wasn’t as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed [Lake’s] writing.â Meanwhile, Remedy and Rockstar have teamed up to remake the first two Max Payne games as a single title, with Remedy developing the new entry using its own tech and Rockstar publishing it. sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Max Payne 3 was a "failure," says Dan Houser, because despite writing GTA games, he's no Sam Lake
sources.text: Whatever you may think of it on its own merits, it's safe to say Max Payne 3 didn't quite live up to the previous two. Being developed by Rockstar instead of Remedy Entertainment, the threequel wound up having a different vibe to the neo-noir stylishness of its predecessors, and looking back on it, lead writer Dan Houser admits the team didn't nail the tone. "It was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured. I really enjoyed that as an experience," he recalled to IGN . "I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen." After leading the narrative departments of many of the Grand Theft Auto games and the first Red Dead Redemption at that point, Houser had some confidence. His belief during development was that the team was nailing what fans wanted - alas, it was not. "I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it," he remembers. "So I got that completely wrong," he says, candidly. "I know [Max Payne creator] Sam Lake well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success." Now that we're 14 years removed, there's a lot to like about the third installment of the series. The gunplay is solid, the setting of Sao Paulo is a fun contrast to the streets of New York City, and the plot is appropriately psychological. But it is a different energy to Remedy's more reserved approach - not exactly surprising given it's Rockstar - and even today, if you play all three Max Payne games one after the other, you'll notice a difference. "The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been," Houser says on reflection. "So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing." Sadly, we're still waiting for Max Payne 4. Remedy's working on remakes of the first two. Whether we'll get the trilogy-ender is in Rockstar's hands. But at least we haven't seen the last of the detective just yet. stories.title: Xbox Announces Xbox Labs, Aimed in Part at Getting Improved Old-Gen Games Playable in Web Browsers
stories.summary: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Xbox Announces Xbox Labs, Aimed in Part at Getting Improved Old-Gen Games Playable in Web Browsers
sources.text: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative aimed at getting games to more people in more places — with a particular emphasis on web browsers. No doubt seeing the growing community of games getting improved versions ported into web browsers (like the 94fps browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved), Microsoft itself is keen to get in on the action in support of new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's goal of reaching 1 billion players per day . Xbox has been tinkering with running Xbox and Xbox 360 games in browsers, and the Xbox Labs initiative is a formalization of those efforts that will see a small team of engineers playing with emerging technologies in order to find new ways for games new and old to be distributed and even created. And IGN understands that this won't just be an R&D effort; rather, Xbox Labs is tasked with shipping products – Sharma says, "We'll build in the open" – and getting gamers to engage with them. I'd suggest thinking about it as a next phase of the backward compatibility efforts that started at Xbox over a decade ago, which the recent disc-to-digital program built on (which, side note, is a much more consumer-friendly path towards the seemingly inevitable digital future than what Sony is doing ), and now Xbox Labs aims to take it even further. It remains to be seen if or how Xbox will look to monetize its Xbox Labs offerings, be it via an upfront cost, in-game microtransactions, or in-game-ad-based revenue . The Xbox Labs announcement continues a busy stretch for Xbox, which revealed its entertainment-industry-focused Xbox XP arm last week. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: Xbox Announces ‘Xbox Labs’, a New Xbox Division to “Explore New Technology”
sources.text: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has today announced ‘Xbox Labs’, a new Xbox division headed by Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet. The announcement was made by Asha Sharma via Xbox’s blog, Xbox Labs will be led by Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet, previously CVP at Microsoft for Azure OpenAI & AI Infrastructure. I’ll be somewhat honest: the announcement is a little confusing, or at the very least, it seems like a way to avoid mentioning the words “Artificial intelligence” or “generative AI”. “These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games,” says Sharma. “While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models,” she continued. The announcement reads awfully like this is yet another company in the video game industry exploring its uses with AI, with Asha Sharma mentioning towards the end of the email that “Our [Xbox’s] priorities aren’t changing.” as she assures developers. RELATED – XBOX Testing a New ‘Streak’ System for Dashboard “We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway,” she said. I’ll admit, though, it’s a little confusing who will actually be using the tools and what limitations they have. Is this AI? Modding? I guess there are a lot more questions to be answered. But I guess time will tell. What do you think of the Xbox Labs news? Let us know your thoughts about the game on the Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.title: Xbox announces Xbox Labs to explore ’emerging technologies’
sources.text: Xbox has announced Xbox Labs, a new initiative focused on exploring ’emerging technologies’ and their potential applications in video games. According to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, the initiative will bring together a small group of game makers, engineers, and scientists to experiment with new ideas, including making games more accessible, giving older games new life, and enabling more players to become creators. Xbox Labs will be led by Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet. Xbox said the group will share the tools it develops with developers across the industry, while emphasizing that its existing priorities remain unchanged, including its commitment to the four Cs , games, hardware, and responsible stewardship of its intellectual property and communities. Read the full announcement from Sharma below. The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make Xbox what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together. In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another. These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up Xbox Labs, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating. I think Xbox has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing Xbox games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have. Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. Labs gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway.

stories.title: 5 jogos exclusivos de PS5 que você não pode perder
stories.summary: Astro Bot, Demon’s Souls, Ghost of Yōtei e outros títulos mostram algumas das experiências que continuam associadas ao console da Sony O post 5 jogos exclusivos de PS5 que você não pode perder apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital Games
sources.title: 5 jogos exclusivos de PS5 que você não pode perder
sources.text: Com cada vez mais jogos da PlayStation chegando ao PC, falar em “exclusivos de PS5” ficou um pouco mais complicado. Títulos como Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 , God of War Ragnarök e Horizon Forbidden West , por exemplo, já podem ser encontrados fora do console. Ainda assim, o PS5 mantém jogos que permanecem ligados à plataforma e ajudam a mostrar diferentes lados do catálogo da Sony . De plataformas a RPGs difíceis, passando por grandes aventuras de mundo aberto, separamos cinco títulos para conhecer. Depois de Astro’s Playroom apresentar gratuitamente algumas das possibilidades do DualSense, Astro Bot transformou a ideia em uma aventura completa. O jogo de plataforma coloca o pequeno robô da PlayStation em dezenas de fases, com mecânicas que mudam constantemente e referências a diferentes momentos da história dos consoles da Sony. O destaque está justamente na variedade. Cada mundo apresenta ideias próprias, enquanto recursos como resposta tátil e gatilhos adaptáveis são incorporados à jogabilidade. Para quem acabou de comprar um PS5, é uma das melhores portas de entrada para entender o que o hardware pode oferecer além de gráficos melhores. O remake de Demon’s Souls , desenvolvido pela Bluepoint Games, reconstruiu o RPG lançado originalmente para PS3 e ajudou a apresentar o potencial técnico do PS5 logo no início da geração. A estrutura, porém, continua bastante fiel ao original. O jogador precisa explorar áreas perigosas, enfrentar inimigos capazes de puni-lo rapidamente e aprender com cada derrota. É uma experiência exigente, mas que recompensa observação, paciência e domínio dos sistemas de combate. Também é uma boa escolha para entender as raízes da fórmula que posteriormente ajudaria a popularizar jogos como Dark Souls e Elden Ring . Ghost of Yōtei leva a fórmula apresentada em Ghost of Tsushima para uma nova história, ambientação e protagonista. Desta vez, acompanhamos Atsu em uma jornada pelo Japão do século XVII, com exploração, confrontos e uma narrativa de vingança no centro da experiência. Um ano após o lançamento, o game também ganhou uma Edição Completa, reunindo a campanha principal, o multiplayer Legends , o modo roguelike Mais Procurados e a expansão narrativa Ecos de Sekigahara . Para quem procura uma aventura extensa no PS5, é uma das opções mais completas atualmente. A Insomniac Games trocou o Homem-Aranha por outro herói da Marvel em Marvel’s Wolverine . O jogo acompanha Logan em uma aventura mais violenta e coloca as famosas garras do personagem no centro de um sistema de combate pensado para transmitir sua força e agressividade. O título também funciona como uma das grandes vitrines da geração do PS5. Para quem gostou do trabalho da Insomniac com Marvel’s Spider-Man , Wolverine é uma escolha natural, mas com identidade própria e uma proposta de combate bem diferente das aventuras de Peter Parker e Miles Morales. James Bond também ganhou uma nova interpretação nos videogames com 007 First Light . Desenvolvido pela IO Interactive, de Hitman , o título apresenta uma versão mais jovem do agente antes de se tornar o famoso 007. A proposta combina espionagem, infiltração, ação e diferentes maneiras de resolver situações, aproveitando a experiência do estúdio com ambientes que oferecem múltiplas possibilidades ao jogador. Para quem gosta de jogos de espionagem, é uma alternativa que foge um pouco dos tradicionais mundos abertos e aventuras de super-heróis. A estratégia da Sony mudou ao longo dos últimos anos, e exclusividade passou a ser um conceito menos definitivo. Jogos que começam restritos ao PlayStation podem posteriormente receber versões para outras plataformas, especialmente PC. Por isso, mais importante do que montar uma biblioteca pensando apenas no selo de “exclusivo” é observar quais experiências fazem sentido para quem tem o console. Astro Bot , Demon’s Souls , Ghost of Yōtei , Marvel’s Wolverine e 007 First Light representam gêneros bastante diferentes e ajudam a mostrar a variedade disponível no PS5. sources.title: Loja pirata traz mais de 1 mil jogos grátis para o PS5 em versão desbloqueada, mas pode dar ban
sources.text: Um novo aplicativo chamado Overdrive foi lançado recentemente para o PlayStation 5 desbloqueado e permite baixar jogos e conteúdos adicionais (DLCs) sem custos. A ferramenta funciona como uma loja digital alternativa para consoles que passaram pelo processo de desbloqueio, violando diretrizes da PlayStation Store. A novidade surge em meio a relatos sobre novas possibilidades abertas pelo jailbreak do PS5. Nas últimas semanas, usuários também demonstraram recursos como a execução de discos de PlayStation 2 no console atual . Vídeos publicados recentemente nas redes sociais mostram o funcionamento do Overdrive e uma biblioteca com mais de mil jogos. Como a ferramenta está associada à pirataria, certamente que os downloads não estão autorizados pelas detentoras dos direitos dos títulos. O Overdrive funciona como uma loja instalada diretamente no PS5 desbloqueado. Por meio da interface, os usuários podem navegar pelo catálogo e selecionar jogos para baixar, sem que a listagem apresente preços. Em vez dos valores normalmente exibidos nas lojas digitais oficiais, a interface mostra informações como o tamanho dos arquivos e a classificação indicativa dos títulos. O aplicativo, portanto, oferece uma experiência semelhante à de uma loja convencional, mas voltada à distribuição não autorizada de jogos. Entre os jogos exibidos nos vídeos estão Battlefield 6 , 007: First Light , Forza Horizon 5 e Black Myth: Wukong . Apesar da quantidade de jogos disponíveis, o funcionamento do Overdrive depende de um console compatível com o desbloqueio. A instalação também não representa uma alternativa oficial à PlayStation Store, e o download de jogos protegidos por direitos autorais sem autorização pode configurar violação de propriedade intelectual. Ou seja, assim como desbloquear o PS5, baixar a loja pode gerar banimento da conta da PSN e do console. Além da distribuição de jogos, o PS5 desbloqueado também recebeu uma ferramenta relacionada ao Xbox Cloud Gaming, serviço de jogos em nuvem da Microsoft. Segundo uma reportagem do WccfTech , o cliente nativo se chama PSXBOX e permite acessar e transmitir títulos no console da Sony. A ferramenta oferece streaming em resolução de até 1080p a 60 quadros por segundo. O cliente também é compatível com o controle DualSense, permitindo utilizar os recursos do acessório durante as partidas. O PSXBOX inclui ainda um menu acessível durante os jogos, com estatísticas e configurações de imagem, resolução de transmissão e opções de upscaling. O funcionamento depende do desbloqueio do console e do acesso ao serviço de jogos em nuvem. O desbloqueio do PlayStation 5 também vem abrindo espaço para projetos de emulação. Entre eles está o PS5CEMU-HAR, ferramenta que adapta emuladores de Wii U e Nintendo 3DS ao console da Sony e permite executar The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild em 4K a 30 FPS . O projeto reúne os emuladores Cemu, voltado a jogos de Wii U, e Azahar, destinado a títulos de Nintendo 3DS. A renderização utiliza a API gráfica Vulkan por meio de uma versão do driver RADV adaptada para o PS5, com suporte ao DualSense. Segundo a descrição do projeto, a ferramenta integra os dois emuladores em uma estrutura própria. “Ele reúne dois emuladores, ambos renderizando com Vulkan através da versão para PS5 do driver RADV feita por Mihawk e executados com o DualSense”, afirma a documentação. No caso do Cemu, o sistema também oferece recursos como renderização em 3840 x 2160, filtros de upscaling, suporte a telas de 120 Hz e pacotes gráficos criados pela comunidade. A compatibilidade e o desempenho variam conforme o jogo e a versão do sistema utilizada. Vale ressaltar que a Sony já corrigiu o exploit que permite desbloquear o PS5 usando o método Relapse, que permite o uso de lojas como o Overdrive e emulação de jogos. No entanto, a solução ainda roda em consoles que não tiveram o firmware atualizado. Ainda assim, para o usuário comum, a dica é ficar longe de soluções como essa, que podem render banimento e até inutilizar o console. O VOXL também ressalta que é contra toda forma de pirataria de games e aconselha jogadores a evitarem processos que podem render violações de direitos autorais. Você acha que o desbloqueio do PS5 e a facilidade de acessar jogos piratas podem mudar o cenário do console? Conte sua opinião nas redes sociais do Voxl ! stories.title: Epic Games reportedly delays Star Wars and Marvel shooter, as the Fortnite maker embraces "AI-accelerated development"
stories.summary: Epic Games has reportedly turned to gen-AI to finish up development on a shooter that crosses over Star Wars and Marvel, which has been internally delayed. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Epic Games reportedly delays Star Wars and Marvel shooter, as the Fortnite maker embraces "AI-accelerated development"
sources.text: Epic Games has reportedly turned to gen-AI to finish up development on a shooter that crosses over Star Wars and Marvel, which has been internally delayed. That's according to a Bloomberg report from journalist Jason Schreier, citing anonymous sources familiar with the unannounced game. Epic's in-development project - a collaboration with Disney - is said to have hit a speed bump, and the Fortnite maker is apparently telling its developers to embrace more gen-AI tools for the rest of the game's production. The new shooter purportedly features characters from both the Marvel and Star Wars series, and the company expected to have it out the door in March 2027. Now that the crossover project has slipped, Epic reportedly told its staff to adopt an "AI first" production pipeline and finish the game with tech such as Anthropic's Claude. In an internal message seen by Bloomberg, one game director told developers there would be "no more hand-written code" and art work should be "generated with full AI workflows" - much to the surprise of many workers. "We're embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do," Epic's communications director, Jake Jones, said in a statement to Bloomberg. "We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration," CEO Tim Sweeney tweeted . "The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal." The Walt Disney company acquired a $1.5b stake in Epic Games a few years back, as the two entertainment giants agreed to partner on a "games and entertainment universe" somehow connected to Fortnite. There weren't any concrete details on the collaboration at the time, though the duo said players would be able to "create their own stories and experiences, express their fandom in a distinctly Disney way, and share content with each other in ways that they love". More recently, it was reported that senior Disney executives were interested in buying Epic Games outright . Epic's push for gen-AI to infiltrate almost all levels of game development comes less than a year after it laid off over 1,000 humans . At the time, CEO Tim Sweeney told staff "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded."

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: Epic shifts to ‘AI-accelerated development’ for upcoming Disney game
sources.text: Developers working on the unannounced shooter game were told to use AI tools like Anthropic’s Claude.﻿ Developers working on the unannounced shooter game were told to use AI tools like Anthropic’s Claude.﻿ Epic Games plans to use AI to generate code and art for an unannounced Disney game, which is now delayed from its original March release window, according to a report from Bloomberg . The project’s developers have been given an “AI-first” mandate directing them to use tools like Anthropic’s Claude more to finish the game. According to Bloomberg , one of the game’s directors said in a message to staff, “No more hand-written code.” Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.” In a statement given to Bloomberg , Epic Games spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI-accelerated development.” Epic Games and Disney did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but Epic CEO Tim Sweeney tweeted : “We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration. The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.” The upcoming game is reportedly a shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars . It’s part of a multiyear collaboration between Epic and Disney, which also invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024. Epic already uses AI in Fortnite , which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader . But it sounds like Epic may be aiming to have AI do most of the heavy lifting on its new Disney game. AI game development tools have been popping up from other large companies, like Meta and Google , so Epic isn’t alone here. Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has also pushed for Steam to drop its “made with AI” tag , arguing that “AI will be involved in nearly all future production.” Earlier this year, Epic laid off over 1,000 of its employees , following a “downturn” in engagement on Fortnite since 2025. Update, October 13th: Added Sweeney’s tweet.

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Usual June delayed to January 20, 2027
sources.text: Finji has delayed supernatural third-person action adventure game Usual June from its previously planned October 28 release date to January 20, 2027. It will be available for PC via Steam . Here is an overview of the game, via Finji: Usual June is a third-person action adventure game where players can fight monsters, talk to ghosts, and most importantly get to the bottom of a mystery threatening to obliterate an entire city. Players will get to explore unique locations such as secret labs, buried tunnels, haunted observatories, abandoned train stations, and a beautiful but mysterious other world. Players will dive into arenas with fast, fluid, and expressive combat. While being able to dash, use super moves, dodge and parry, players will have to adapt to enemies and change June’s fighting style by equipping items and customizing loadout. As players get more XP and level up, they will gain access to new powers. But these powers come with a cost they will have to discover by themselves. As neither the living nor the dead can save this city on their own, players will get to talk to a colorful cast of 25 characters to get to the bottom of what is happening in Fen Harbor, using the photographic memories of the dead, and the living’s ability to touch things to find out what is happening before all the ghosts disappear and time runs out. Developed by the Finji team, Usual June is led by creative director Adam Saltsman ( Overland , Canabalt ), and produced in collaboration with writer David Pinckney ( Needle & Thread ), BAFTA winning writer Cara Ellison ( Ghost Town , The Seance of Blake Manor ) and BAFTA winning audio director Adam Hay ( Dreams , Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture ).

sources.text: “Death row inmates reality show x death game adventure” game BUZZ or DIE will launch PC via Steam on October 28, publisher Kodansha and developer Bon announced . It will support English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese language options. A demo is available now. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : BUZZ or DIE is a point-and-click game where death row inmates enter a death-match game show. You and a man named Sagishima will be participating together. The rules are simple. Dive into your opponent’s mindscape and search for secrets. Turn those secrets into content and make a short video. Gain the most Likes from the audience to win. The winner receives a pardon and the chance to have one wish granted. The loser receives not only death…but an eternity of humiliation as a slave android model. Witness the passions and fury of the world’s worst criminals in this gripping video-game drama. We hope you enjoy.
